payload.summary: Independently verified all five amendments against the current codebase. Three amendments (fr-1-008e032a, fr-1-7e77d2a4, fr-1-905ce34d) identify genuine gaps or bugs confirmed by code inspection. Two amendments (fr-1-0afb1776, fr-1-e1c5d607) make factually incorrect claims about issues that do not exist — the code they reference has already been correctly updated.

votes.rationale: Verified: the test concentration_kinetics_are_volume_independent in cycling.rs asserts per-liter deltas for TAN, NO2, NO3, DOC, and DON only. There are zero assertions for dissolved oxygen or alkalinity per-liter deltas. The nitrogen_cycle.rs code has explicit DO budget depletion paths (do_budget initialized from dissolved_oxygen_mg_total, debited by AOB/NOB/comammox O2 costs) and alkalinity debit paths (alk_budget initialized from alkalinity_meq_total, debited by alk_per_mg_n costs). These operate on total-mass quantities derived from concentration-based Monod rates, so a volume-dependent bookkeeping bug in these paths would pass undetected. Adding DO and alkalinity per-liter delta assertions is a legitimate test coverage improvement.

Verified: the primary test (lines 632-681) explicitly computes Monod factors (S/(S+K)) for TAN, NO2, DOC, DO_AOB, and DO_decomp across both tank sizes and asserts they match within 1e-12 tolerance. The extreme-scale test (lines 753-872) with a 1000x volume ratio (1L vs 1000L) completely omits this Monod factor verification — it only checks concentration deltas. Since extreme volume ratios could expose floating-point precision issues in Monod factor computation that the 10x ratio test would miss, adding the same Monod factor comparison block to the extreme test is a reasonable and valuable improvement.

The amendment's claim that cargo check -p tank_data fails with E0609 is factually incorrect. The validation code at presets.rs:1584-1610 correctly uses the NEW field names (self.decomposer_k_doc_mg_c_per_l, self.aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l, self.nob_k_nitrite_mg_n_per_l, self.comammox_k_tan_mg_n_per_l). The old field names appear only in TOML test strings, which are correctly deserialized via serde aliases defined on the struct fields (e.g., alias = "decomposer_k_doc_mg" on decomposer_k_doc_mg_c_per_l). Test assignments also use the new field names. The crate builds successfully — there is no E0609 error.

The amendment's claim that parse_process_params_preset only rewrites legacy plant keys is factually incorrect. The normalize_legacy_process_params_preset function at presets.rs:1242-1262 explicitly handles both algae_half_saturation_n_mg_total and algae_half_saturation_p_mg_total, converting them via legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l (divides by 20L reference volume) into algae_half_saturation_n_mg_n_per_l and algae_half_saturation_p_mg_p_per_l respectively. A regression test test_process_preset_parser_migrates_legacy_algae_half_saturation_keys exists at lines 2489+. The normalization path and tests the amendment requests already exist and are complete.

All four claims verified: (1) resolved_colonizable_area_factor at substrate.rs:44-49 checks `> 0.0`, treating exactly 0.0 as missing and falling back to kind defaults (InertSand:0.5, InertGravel:0.6, etc.); (2) refresh_habitat_registry at state.rs:265 writes `resolved_colonizable_area_factor()` back into `layer.colonizable_area_factor`, permanently overwriting the original value in saved state; (3) substrate preset validation at presets.rs:290-328 only rejects `< 0.0`, explicitly allowing 0.0 as valid; (4) migrate_v6_to_v7 at save.rs:660-672 hard-codes kind defaults (0.5/0.6/0.8/0.9) without considering any custom saved values. This creates a real data-integrity bug: a user deliberately setting colonizable_area_factor to 0.0 to disable colonization has their value silently replaced on every refresh and migration. The fix — falling back only when the field is absent or non-finite — is correct.
